guideIntro: Five steps, with an editable example. Keep this guide open while you work.
guideBody1: Load the example to start with the colorful background, three archetypes and demonstration images. To use only the background in your own project, download it and upload it under Static images → Background.
guideTip1: You can also follow these steps with your own project. Loading the example replaces the current project in the editor; save your work first.
guideBody2: In the left panel, go to Title → Text. Replace RETROFORMATS DEMO with your event name and add its date. Keep 8P for this exercise: the example represents eight players.
guideTip2: The title is plain text. The player total in it does not update automatically when you change the slice values.
guideBody3: Under Slices, select an archetype. In Selected slice, edit Label and Slice value. Try Chaos Turbo = 4, Warrior = 3 and Burn = 1. Use player counts, not percentages: the chart calculates each share.
guideTip3: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 players: 50%, 37.5% and 12.5%. After changing counts, check that the labels still fit around the chart.
guideBody4: Select a slice, then click Slice on a library image to assign it. Drag the selected image on the canvas to frame it; use its handles or the mouse wheel to resize it. To combine artworks, use Add image under Slice images.
guideTip4: The geometric images are placeholders. Replace them with your artworks by uploading to the library or using the image search. Check the selected slice and image layer before assigning an image.
guideBody5: Open Preview PNG to check the result without selection handles. Use Save template as to keep an editable .dhbreakdown project. Use Export PNG to download the finished image.
guideTip5: Keep both files: .dhbreakdown for future edits and PNG for sharing. Editor zoom and theme do not change the exported image or its 1080 × 1080 size in this example.
guideBackgroundAlt: Colorful abstract background with a light center and coral, blue, turquoise and yellow edges
guideReplaceConfirm: Load the guide example? It will replace the current project in the editor. Save any work you want to keep first. Files on your computer will not be changed.
